job.title: Senior Lettings Negotiator
job.description:
An established and growing residential property business is looking for an experienced Senior Lettings Negotiator to join its Dublin-based team.

This is a hands-on role for an experienced property professional who is confident managing the full lettings process, building strong relationships with landlords and tenants, and taking ownership of a residential portfolio.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to work across both new development lease-ups and established residential properties, playing an important role in maintaining occupancy levels and delivering a high standard of service.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the end-to-end lettings process across a portfolio of residential properties

  • Support the lease-up of new residential developments

  • Conduct property viewings and negotiate rental terms

  • Manage tenant applications, referencing and onboarding

  • Prepare tenancy agreements and coordinate move-ins

  • Conduct rent reviews in line with current legislation

  • Manage licence renewals and ensure statutory requirements are met

  • Carry out property inspections and prepare condition reports

  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date property and tenant records

  • Provide regular portfolio updates and reporting to clients

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with landlords, tenants and external stakeholders

  • Work closely with property management, maintenance and finance teams to resolve issues efficiently

  • Maintain a strong understanding of Irish residential lettings legislation and regulatory requirements

  • Identify opportunities to improve occupancy, customer experience and portfolio performance

What We're Looking For

  • Proven experience in residential lettings or property management

  • PSRA Category C licence – essential

  • Full clean driving licence and access to your own car – essential

  • Strong knowledge of the Residential Tenancies Act and Irish residential property legislation

  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills

  • Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail

  • Commercially minded and proactive, with a practical approach to problem-solving

  • Comfortable managing multiple properties, tenants and competing priorities

  • Strong Excel skills

  • Experience with property management/lettings systems

Why Consider This Opportunity?

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Lettings Negotiator or Property Manager looking to take on a more senior, commercially focused position within a growing residential property business.

You'll have significant ownership of your portfolio, work closely with internal and external stakeholders, and play a key role in the successful leasing and management of residential assets across Dublin.

Interested?

If you have the relevant property experience and PSRA Category C licence and would like to find out more, please get in touch for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Supervising Pharmacist
job.description:
Supervising Pharmacist – New Pharmacy Opening in Galway

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Supervising Pharmacist to join a brand-new pharmacy opening in Galway.

This is a full-time, permanent position with Sundays off, offering the successful candidate the unique opportunity to play a key role in the launch and development of a new pharmacy. You will be involved in the pharmacy fit-out, operational setup, regulatory documentation, and the establishment of best-in-class pharmacy services from day one.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the day-to-day operation of the dispensary in accordance with all legal and professional requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with PSI regulations, pharmacy legislation, professional ethics, and codes of practice.
  • Provide a safe, accurate, and efficient dispensing service to all patients and customers.
  • Ensure the safe and effective supply of medicines and healthcare advice.
  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with patients, healthcare professionals, and the wider community.
  • Oversee all monthly claims and submissions.
  • Contribute to the pharmacy's continued growth and success
  • Proactively identify and resolve rejected claims.
  • Lead, motivate, and support a strong team of Pharmacy Technicians and OTCs.

Requirements

  • PSI-approved Pharmacy qualification with current registration to practise in the Republic of Ireland.
  • Minimum of 3 years’ post-registration experience.
  • Strong experience in a busy community pharmacy environment.
  • Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
  • Strong leadership and team management capabilities.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work efficiently in a high-volume dispensing setting.
  • Commercial awareness and sound business acumen.
  • A customer-focused approach with a commitment to delivering exceptional patient care.
  • Experience with MPS dispensing software and robotic dispensing systems is desirable.

What is on Offer?

  • Opportunity to lead a brand-new pharmacy from its opening.
  • Full-time permanent role.
  • Sundays off.
  • Supportive working environment.
  • Excellent opportunity for career progression and leadership development.

For a confidential discussion or further information, please forward your CV here.

If you know a pharmacist who may be interested in this opportunity, please feel free to share this vacancy within your network.

job.title: Health & Safety Manager
job.description:
Are you an experienced Health & Safety Manager with a strong manufacturing background and the leadership skills to take full ownership of Health & Safety across a busy site?

Our client, a well-established manufacturing organisation in East Cork, is seeking an experienced Health & Safety Manager to lead the site H&S function.

This is a standalone H&S leadership role, with responsibility for the full Health & Safety function across the plant. You will work closely with senior management, Production, Engineering, Quality and other key departments to drive a strong safety culture, compliance and continuous improvement across the organisation.

What you will be doing:

  • Lead and own the site Health & Safety strategy, policies, procedures and improvement programmes.
  • Develop and maintain robust Safety Management Systems, ensuring compliance with legislation and industry best practice.
  • Take a proactive leadership role in developing a strong safety culture and safety ownership across all levels of the organisation.
  • Work closely with Production, Engineering, Quality and other departments to identify risks and implement practical improvements.
  • Monitor H&S performance through KPIs, incident reporting, trend analysis and action plans.
  • Lead the investigation of incidents and ensure effective corrective and preventative actions are implemented.
  • Regularly review and update Risk Assessments, Safety Statements, SOPs and safe systems of work.
  • Develop and deliver H&S training, employee inductions and awareness programmes.
  • Identify training requirements arising from legislation, operational changes and site activities.
  • Provide H&S reports, metrics and recommendations to the management team.
  • Ensure effective H&S documentation, record keeping and document control.
  • Promote lessons learned, best practice and continuous improvement across the site.
  • Work with the site Health & Safety Committee and key stakeholders to drive improvements in safety performance.
  • Act as a visible H&S leader, influencing and challenging at all levels to ensure safety standards are maintained.

What we are looking for:

  • A third-level qualification in Health & Safety or a related discipline.
  • 7+ years’ experience in Health & Safety, ideally within a manufacturing environment.
  • Manufacturing experience is essential.
  • Strong knowledge of Health & Safety legislation and practical risk management.
  • Proven experience developing and implementing Safety Management Systems.
  • Strong knowledge and experience of ISO 45001, including implementation and auditing.
  • Proven ability to influence senior stakeholders and gain buy-in across different departments.
  • Experience leading H&S programmes and delivering measurable improvements.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to challenge unsafe practices.
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving ability.
  • A proactive, practical approach with the ability to work independently and take full ownership of the H&S function.

What is on offer:

  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Monday to Friday working week.
  • Company pension.
  • Education assistance.
  • Company events.
  • Discretionary sick pay.
  • A genuine site leadership position with full H&S responsibility.
  • Opportunity to shape and develop the safety culture within an established manufacturing organisation.
  • Long-term career opportunity within a well-established business.

If you are an experienced Health & Safety Manager with strong manufacturing experience and are ready to take full ownership of H&S within an established manufacturing site in East Cork, apply today with your CV.

job.description:
FRS Recruitment is now inviting applications for the role of Agricultural Consultant on behalf of our client, to support farmers and landowners across Limerick, Tipperary and Clare.

This role provides extensive training and mentoring, making it an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build a long-term career in agricultural consultancy while maintaining a strong connection to practical farming.

Key Responsibilities

  • Advising farmers on Department of Agriculture schemes and supports, including:
    • BISS, Eco Schemes, TAMS, ACRES
  • Preparation and submission of scheme applications.
  • Nutrient Management Planning.
  • Soil sampling and fertiliser recommendations.
  • Preparation of County Council and planning-related reports.
  • Providing general farm business and compliance advice.
  • Building relationships with clients and responding to day-to-day farm queries.
  • Managing a client caseload while working both independently and collaboratively within the consultancy team.

Ideal Candidate

The client is open to a range of backgrounds and experience levels, with strong support available for the right person.

Suitable candidates may include:

  • Individuals currently working in agricultural advisory, agri-services or farm support roles.
  • Farmers or relief farmers looking to diversify their career while remaining involved in farming.
  • Agricultural professionals seeking a flexible role that offers a strong work-life balance.
  • Graduates also considered

Essential Requirements

  • Level 8 qualification in Agriculture or a related discipline.
  • Good understanding of Irish farming systems and environmental regulations.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Competent IT skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
  • Full clean driving licence.
  • DAFM FAS approval, or willingness to obtain approval at the next available opportunity.

Working Arrangement

The role offers a flexible mix of:

  • Home-based working.
  • On-farm client visits.
  • Occasional office attendance.

During peak periods, particularly in spring, attendance in the office may be required approximately 1-2 days per week. The remainder of the role can largely be managed remotely and through farm visits.

The successful candidate will have the autonomy to manage their own workload and develop their own client relationships, while benefiting from the support of an experienced consultancy team.

Training & Development

  • Full training provided.
  • Structured mentoring programme.
  • Significant support during the first 12-24 months.
  • Opportunity to gradually build and manage an independent client portfolio.
  • Long-term career progression within the business.

Package

  • Salary: Negotiable
  • Mileage and subsistence paid.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • Full-time position (37.5 hours per week).
  • Part-time hours will also be considered for the right candidate, particularly someone actively involved in farming.

Why This Role May Appeal

This opportunity is particularly well suited to someone who wants the best of both worlds: a professional career in agricultural consultancy while retaining time for their own farming enterprise. The flexibility, home-working arrangement, strong mentoring and variety of advisory work make it an attractive option for graduates, junior consultants and practical farmers alike.

job.description:
Contract Psychologist – Neurodevelopmental Assessments

Location: Dublin
Contract: Contract / Part-Time
Hours: Flexible
Rates: Excellent rates available

We are seeking an experienced Clinical, Counselling or Educational Psychologist to join a supportive, multidisciplinary team providing high-quality, evidence-based neurodevelopmental assessments to children, young people and families.

This is an excellent part-time contract opportunity offering flexible working arrangements and competitive rates, making it ideal for an experienced Psychologist looking for greater flexibility alongside other professional commitments.

You will play a key role in delivering comprehensive assessments across Autism, ADHD, Intellectual Disability and other neurodevelopmental presentations, working collaboratively with an experienced MDT and senior clinicians.

The Role

As a Contract Psychologist, you will be responsible for:

  • Conducting face-to-face structured observations as part of neurodevelopmental assessments.
  • Completing remote developmental history interviews with parents and carers.
  • Contributing to collaborative MDT diagnostic discussions with support from senior clinicians.
  • Providing clear, compassionate feedback to children, young people and families.
  • Preparing high-quality clinical reports and diagnostic formulations.
  • Applying your expertise in differential diagnosis and evidence-based practice.

What You Can Expect

  • Excellent contract rates
  • Part-time and flexible hours
  • Optimised Diary planning in line with your preferences
  • A supportive and highly collaborative multidisciplinary team
  • Access to innovative digital tools designed to reduce administration and support efficient report writing
  • Comprehensive onboarding and training on clinical systems
  • Dedicated IT and operational support
  • Opportunities to contribute to training, research and professional development initiatives
  • A values-led environment focused on clinical excellence, compassion and staff wellbeing

Requirements

We are looking for Psychologists with:

  • A recognised Level 8 Psychology qualification or equivalent.
  • A postgraduate professional qualification recognised by the Psychological Society of Ireland (PSI) in Clinical or Counselling Psychology, or an appropriate recognised qualification in Educational Psychology.
  • A minimum of 3 years' experience conducting diagnostic assessments for Autism, ADHD and/or other neurodevelopmental conditions.
  • Strong knowledge of DSM-5 diagnostic criteria and differential diagnosis.
  • Experience conducting cognitive and neurodevelopmental assessments.
  • Training and experience using diagnostic tools such as ADOS-2 and ADI-R.
  • Excellent clinical report-writing skills.
  • Strong communication skills and a compassionate approach when working with children, young people and families.
  • The ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Excellent organisation and time-management skills.
  • Eligibility to work in the Republic of Ireland.

An Excellent Flexible Opportunity

This is an opportunity to join a forward-thinking clinical service where you can focus on delivering high-quality psychological care while benefiting from flexible working, excellent contract rates and strong clinical support.

If you are an experienced Psychologist with a background in neurodevelopmental assessment and are interested in a flexible part-time contract in Dublin, I would be very interested in hearing from you.

job.title: Education & Training Officer
job.description:
Training & Education Officer

FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Training & Education Officer to lead the development and delivery of education, training and awareness initiatives across the organisation and wider community.

Role Purpose

The Training & Education Officer will develop and deliver high-quality training and awareness programmes that promote understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women, children and young people.

The role will build knowledge and skills across Aoibhneas, partner organisations and the wider community through training, education, awareness initiatives and professional engagement. The postholder will also represent the organisation and contribute to service development and best practice.

Key Responsibilities

Training & Education

  • Develop, coordinate and deliver training for staff, volunteers, students and external stakeholders.
  • Design and maintain training materials, presentations, guidance and learning resources.
  • Deliver training on domestic abuse, safeguarding, trauma-informed practice, coercive control, risk assessment, child protection and related areas.
  • Develop annual training plans aligned with organisational priorities and legislative requirements.
  • Evaluate training effectiveness and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain accurate training records and support compliance with mandatory learning requirements.
  • Work with managers to identify learning and development needs.

Community Awareness & Engagement

  • Deliver workshops, presentations, information sessions and awareness initiatives to schools, community groups, statutory agencies and voluntary organisations.
  • Promote understanding of domestic abuse and best practice responses within communities and professional networks.
  • Represent Aoibhneas at conferences, forums, community events and professional networks.
  • Develop accessible educational and information resources.
  • Support local and national awareness initiatives relating to domestic abuse and violence against women.

Service Development

  • Research emerging trends, evidence and best practice to inform training and programme development.
  • Identify training and knowledge gaps across services and partner organisations.
  • Contribute to the development of policies, procedures and practice guidance.
  • Support specialist programmes for women, children and young people affected by domestic abuse.
  • Contribute to quality improvement and organisational learning.

Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop and maintain positive relationships with statutory agencies, schools, colleges, community organisations and professional networks.
  • Support collaborative initiatives and referral pathways.
  • Participate in relevant interagency groups, committees and professional networks.
  • Strengthen partnership approaches to domestic abuse prevention and response.

Administration & Reporting

  • Maintain accurate records of training delivery, attendance and outcomes.
  • Prepare reports, statistics and evaluation data.
  • Assist with funding reports, monitoring requirements and service evaluations.
  • Maintain training databases and learning management systems where applicable.
  • Liaise with the Head of Services regarding priorities and programme development.

Other Duties

  • Participate in relevant training and continuous professional development.
  • Work collaboratively across Aoibhneas to support organisational objectives.
  • Represent Aoibhneas professionally and maintain high standards of practice.
  • Undertake other duties appropriate to the role as assigned by the Head of Services or CEO.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Degree-level qualification in Education, Training, Social Care, Community Development, Social Science, Adult Education or a related discipline.
  • Minimum three years' relevant experience in training, education, social care, community development or a related setting.
  • Strong knowledge and understanding of domestic abuse and its impact on women and children.
  • Proven experience designing, delivering and evaluating training programmes.
  • Excellent facilitation, presentation and communication skills.
  • Experience developing training materials and learning resources.
  • Strong organisational and administrative skills.
  • Excellent report-writing and data management abilities.
  • Experience working with partners and external stakeholders.
  • Full driving licence.

Desirable

  • Qualification or accreditation in training/adult education.
  • Knowledge of Children First and safeguarding requirements.
  • Experience delivering training within the domestic abuse, social care or community sector.
  • Experience of interagency working.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Integrity and dependability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.
  • Strong self-management and emotional resilience.

Role Requirements

The role will require flexibility to work across Aoibhneas and community locations, with regular travel to educational, community and organisational settings.

Working hours will generally be five days per week between 9.00am and 6.00pm, with occasional evening or weekend work required to facilitate training, awareness events and community engagement activities.

A full driving licence is essential.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

All offers of employment with Aoibhneas are subject to Garda Vetting, satisfactory reference checks and verification of legal eligibility to work in Ireland. Aoibhneas is an equal opportunities employer. A panel may be formed from this recruitment process.

job.title: Agricultural Consultant
job.description:
FRS Recruitment is now inviting applications for the role of Agricultural Consultant on behalf of our client, to support farmers and landowners across Limerick, Tipperary and Clare.

This role provides extensive training and mentoring, making it an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build a long-term career in agricultural consultancy while maintaining a strong connection to practical farming.

Key Responsibilities

  • Advising farmers on Department of Agriculture schemes and supports, including:
    • BISS, Eco Schemes, TAMS, ACRES
  • Preparation and submission of scheme applications.
  • Nutrient Management Planning.
  • Soil sampling and fertiliser recommendations.
  • Preparation of County Council and planning-related reports.
  • Providing general farm business and compliance advice.
  • Building relationships with clients and responding to day-to-day farm queries.
  • Managing a client caseload while working both independently and collaboratively within the consultancy team.

Ideal Candidate

The client is open to a range of backgrounds and experience levels, with strong support available for the right person.

Suitable candidates may include:

  • Individuals currently working in agricultural advisory, agri-services or farm support roles.
  • Farmers or relief farmers looking to diversify their career while remaining involved in farming.
  • Agricultural professionals seeking a flexible role that offers a strong work-life balance.
  • Graduates also considered

Essential Requirements

  • Level 8 qualification in Agriculture or a related discipline.
  • Good understanding of Irish farming systems and environmental regulations.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
  • Competent IT skills.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a small team.
  • Full clean driving licence.
  • DAFM FAS approval, or willingness to obtain approval at the next available opportunity.

Working Arrangement

The role offers a flexible mix of:

  • Home-based working.
  • On-farm client visits.
  • Occasional office attendance.

During peak periods, particularly in spring, attendance in the office may be required approximately 1-2 days per week. The remainder of the role can largely be managed remotely and through farm visits.

The successful candidate will have the autonomy to manage their own workload and develop their own client relationships, while benefiting from the support of an experienced consultancy team.

Training & Development

  • Full training provided.
  • Structured mentoring programme.
  • Significant support during the first 12-24 months.
  • Opportunity to gradually build and manage an independent client portfolio.
  • Long-term career progression within the business.

Package

  • Salary: Negotiable
  • Mileage and subsistence paid.
  • Flexible working arrangements.
  • Full-time position (37.5 hours per week).
  • Part-time hours will also be considered for the right candidate, particularly someone actively involved in farming.

Why This Role May Appeal

This opportunity is particularly well suited to someone who wants the best of both worlds: a professional career in agricultural consultancy while retaining time for their own farming enterprise. The flexibility, home-working arrangement, strong mentoring and variety of advisory work make it an attractive option for graduates, junior consultants and practical farmers alike.

How to Apply

Apply today by submitting your CV application through the below link

All Applications treated with 100% confidentiality

job.title: Quality Manager
job.description:
Quality Manager-Cork

Excellent salary package + bonus, pension & healthcare

Please note: This position is open to candidates who already have the legal right to work in Ireland. Visa sponsorship or work permit support is not available for this position.

A well-established Cork based food manufacturer is continuing to expand its operations and is now seeking an experienced Quality Manager to join the team.

The business manufactures a wide range of nutritional products serving multiple sectors, with a strong focus on quality, food/feed safety, compliance and continuous improvement.

The business is undergoing significant expansion, including the construction of a new production facility and a major increase in manufacturing capacity. This is an excellent opportunity to play a key role in developing and strengthening the Quality function as the business grows.

Reporting to the Operations Manager, you will be responsible for:

  • Lead and manage the Quality function across all manufacturing operations, ensuring strong quality performance, product release and robust compliance systems.
  • Maintain effective traceability and batch record systems, ensuring accuracy, integrity and accessibility of records.
  • Lead regulatory and certification compliance, ensuring adherence to DAFM, HACCP, UFAS, NOPS, GMP+ and relevant customer and industry standards.
  • Manage the Quality Management System (QMS) and document control processes.
  • Develop and oversee the analytical testing programme, using HACCP and risk assessment principles.
  • Lead the internal audit programme and manage all external audits and regulatory inspections, ensuring findings are addressed promptly.
  • Oversee supplier approval, raw material change control and cross-functional assessment of quality and regulatory impacts.
  • Manage the customer complaints process, ensuring effective investigation, corrective action and timely closure.
  • Lead non-conformance, root cause analysis and corrective action, driving continuous improvement across the site.
  • Monitor and trend key quality and site performance metrics, leading quality review meetings and follow-up actions.
  • Develop team capability through effective training, coaching and support.
  • Work closely with Operations, Technical, Commercial and other functions to deliver site objectives and maintain high standards of quality and compliance.

Experience & Skills

  • Prior experience as a Quality Manager in a production processing environment
  • 10 years minimum experience in a pharma or food production environment.
  • Degree in a Science related subject
  • Level 5 or higher HACCP certification
  • Strong leadership and management skills
  • Excellent understanding of Food Safety and Quality Management Systems, with strong knowledge of food/feed legislation, customer standards and Codes of Practice
  • Formal Audit Training / Lead Auditor or Internal Auditor experience

What's in it for you?

  • Excellent salary package DOE
  • Performance-related bonus
  • Pension
  • Healthcare
  • Opportunity to join a business undergoing significant expansion
  • Major investment in a new production facility
  • Opportunity to play a key role in developing and strengthening the Quality function as the business grows

Please note: This position is open to candidates who already have the legal right to work in Ireland. Visa sponsorship or work permit support is not available for this position.

job.title: CNS- Respiratory
job.description:
Respiratory Clinical Nurse Specialist

Are you an experienced nurse with specialist expertise in respiratory care and a passion for developing high-quality, patient-centred services?

We are seeking an ambitious, innovative and highly motivated Respiratory Clinical Nurse Specialist (CNS) to establish and lead a new Respiratory Specialist Nursing Service within our acute private hospital.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced respiratory nurse to take a leading role in shaping and developing a specialist service from the ground up. Working alongside our established respiratory experts, the successful candidate will develop a patient-centred CNS service designed to enhance clinical outcomes, promote excellence in respiratory care and support the strategic development of respiratory services across the hospital.

Working collaboratively with Consultant Respiratory Physicians, Nursing Leadership, Allied Health Professionals and wider multidisciplinary teams, the Respiratory CNS will play a key role in developing and implementing evidence-based pathways of care for patients with a broad range of respiratory conditions.

These will include, but are not limited to:

  • Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD)

  • Asthma

  • Bronchiectasis

  • Interstitial Lung Disease (ILD)

  • Other acute and chronic respiratory conditions

The successful candidate will also contribute to patient optimisation, education, care coordination, clinical governance, quality improvement and the ongoing development of respiratory nursing practice.

Essential Qualifications & Experience

Applicants must demonstrate:

  • Current registration as a Registered General Nurse on the General Division of the Register maintained by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland (NMBI).

  • A minimum of five years’ post-registration clinical experience.

  • At least two years’ recent experience in respiratory nursing or a relevant respiratory clinical specialty.

  • A Level 8 qualification in Nursing.

  • Evidence of ongoing continuing professional development (CPD) relevant to respiratory care.

  • Experience in service development, project management and/or quality improvement.

  • Completion of, or willingness to undertake, relevant education and professional development in Clinical Nurse Specialist practice.

Desirable Qualifications & Experience

The following would be advantageous:

  • A Master’s degree in Nursing, Healthcare or a related discipline.

  • Nurse Prescribing qualification, or a willingness to undertake the qualification.

  • Experience in the development and delivery of comprehensive patient and family education programmes focused on respiratory illness, self-management and patient optimisation.

  • Experience in developing and implementing clinical pathways, protocols and evidence-based respiratory care programmes.

  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams and contribute to service innovation.

The Opportunity

This is an opportunity to make a significant contribution to the development of a new specialist respiratory nursing service, while working closely with an established multidisciplinary respiratory team.

job.title: CNC Service Engineer
job.description:
CNC Service Engineer

Galway / Limerick | Field Based | Company Vehicle

A leading precision engineering solutions company is seeking a CNC Service Engineer to join its growing field service team. This is a nationwide field-based position, with candidates ideally located in Galway, Limerick or the surrounding areas.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced CNC Service Engineer, Maintenance Technician or Mechatronic Technician who enjoys fault finding and wants to develop specialist expertise within CNC machine tool technology.

The Role

Working as part of an experienced team of Field Service Engineers, you will provide technical support to customers throughout Ireland, covering the installation, servicing, maintenance and repair of CNC equipment.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Electrical and mechanical fault finding on CNC machinery
  • Diagnosing and repairing mechanical and electrical faults
  • Installation and commissioning of CNC equipment
  • Carrying out annual servicing and preventative maintenance
  • Providing technical support to customers
  • Liaising with equipment manufacturers and suppliers to resolve technical issues
  • Reading and interpreting electrical and mechanical schematics

The Candidate

Ideally, you will have previous experience working with CNC machinery, PLC-controlled manufacturing equipment or within an industrial maintenance environment.

You should have:

  • Strong electrical and mechanical fault-finding experience
  • Experience working with CNC and/or PLC-controlled manufacturing equipment
  • A good understanding of electrical and mechanical systems
  • Some knowledge of electronics
  • The ability to read and interpret technical schematics
  • Good computer literacy
  • Strong communication and customer-facing skills
  • Good written and spoken English
  • A full driving licence

Experience with hydraulic and pneumatic systems would be an advantage, as would an understanding of CNC code or Ladder Logic.

A Level 5 qualification in a mechanical or electrical discipline, or a recognised mechanical, electrical or mechatronic apprenticeship, would also be beneficial.

Why Apply?

This is an excellent opportunity to develop your career within a highly specialised area of advanced manufacturing technology. You will work alongside experienced CNC Service Engineers and receive ongoing technical development, including opportunities to travel internationally for manufacturer training.

For further information contact Kerry Rickard.

job.title: Delivery Manager
job.description:
ABOUT TURAS NUA

At Turas Nua, we support people who are unemployed by providing intensive, targeted and personalised employment support services. The Intreo Partner of National Employment Services (IPNES) contract is delivered by Turas Nua, the Irish employability services provider. Turas Nua is an Irish employability services provider, wholly owned by FRS Network, an Irish cooperative social enterprise, which has been delivering services to Irish communities since 1980.

ABOUT DEPARTMENT

Our Operations Team support clients through a progression journey towards employment. Our teams provide one-to-one support to clients while coordinating interventions to tackle any barriers to employment.

PURPOSE OF ROLE

As Delivery Manager, you will support, coach & mentor your team of caseworkers to provide the best customer service to our clients. You will understand the contract KPI’s and key objectives and will ensure that your team are working in a way that aims to achieve those KPI’s. You will manage a team across multiple offices and will be expected to travel to each office to provide regular one to one and team meeting time with your teams.

PERSON PROFILE

You will need to be able to lead, motivate, develop, and manage a team of Caseworkers. In particular, you will be responsible for leading and empowering the team to create and embed a culture of high performance, coaching and cross functional working.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  1. Lead, motivate, develop and performance manage the team to continuously improve and increase their capability and deliver against their targets.
  2. Lead and empower the team to support and embed a culture of high quality, and full contractual compliance at all times.
  3. Drive a high-performance culture throughout your team while ensuring a positive working environment.
  4. Undertake regular reviews with Caseworkers, by way of one-to-one meetings, team meetings and optimizing every opportunity for coaching, mentoring, supporting and developing your team.
  5. Manage day to day contact with key stakeholders at a local level, maintaining a positive working relationship across the business.
  6. Partner with HR and Operations Manager effectively manage people issues, recruitment, onboarding, disciplinaries, performance management issues, monitor attrition rates etc.
  7. Conduct coaching session with team so that standards are understood and observed by all Caseworkers, ensuring all clients are provided with the same high standard of service to maximize our clients’ chances of securing sustainable employment.
  8. Prepare for, participate in, and implement recommendations resulting from, DSP inspections.
  9. Investigate, prepare, and respond to Stage 1 customer complaints, TD correspondence REPs and PQs.
  10. Responsible for the operation and arranging maintenance of the facilities of all sites under your remit, ensuring the highest standard of Health and safety for all, in line with company policy.

ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Experience managing a team to meet all KPIs
  • Experience of dealing with challenging customers and resolving conflict situations calmly.
  • Have experience in recruiting, coaching, and developing a diverse and inclusive team
  • Have a good understanding and demonstration of a Growth Mindset
  • Ability to develop and implemented strategies and plans to promote continuous improvement that drives performance
  • Experience in the use of Microsoft office packages.
  • Excellent team player – experience of working successfully as part of a team.
  • Highly efficient.
  • Excellent attention to detail.
  • Flexible and approachable.
  • Detailed understanding of the local/regional support services

Recruiter: Joyce Coffey

job.title: Facilities Supervisor - 12 month contract
job.description:
FRS is delighted to be partnering with Aoibhneas in the recruitment of a Facilities Supervisor to oversee the maintenance, safety, security and operational management of Aoibhneas properties, facilities and accommodation sites. This is a 12 month contract role.

Facilities Management

  • Oversee the day-to-day management and maintenance of Aoibhneas properties, accommodation units, offices and service locations.
  • Ensure premises are safe, secure, well maintained and fit for purpose.
  • Develop and manage preventative maintenance schedules and conduct regular site inspections.
  • Coordinate repairs, maintenance and refurbishment works.
  • Manage access control, keyholding and building security arrangements.
  • Maintain accurate maintenance, inspection, servicing and compliance records.

Health, Safety & Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with relevant Health & Safety legislation and organisational policies.
  • Conduct and review risk assessments relating to buildings, equipment and workplace activities.
  • Monitor fire safety systems, emergency lighting, alarms, extinguishers and evacuation procedures.
  • Ensure statutory inspections, certifications and servicing are completed and recorded.
  • Support emergency planning and business continuity arrangements.
  • Investigate and report facilities-related incidents, hazards, accidents and near misses.
  • Promote a strong culture of safety and continuous improvement.

Contractor & Supplier Management

  • Source, appoint and manage contractors and service providers in line with procurement requirements.
  • Monitor contractor performance, service agreements, costs and value for money.
  • Ensure contractors comply with Health & Safety, safeguarding and organisational requirements.
  • Obtain quotations and support facilities-related procurement.
  • Maintain effective relationships with suppliers, landlords, maintenance providers and utility companies.

Asset & Resource Management

  • Maintain an accurate asset register across all sites.
  • Oversee furniture, equipment, fixtures and operational supplies.
  • Plan asset and equipment replacement programmes.
  • Support budgeting, forecasting and monitoring of facilities expenditure.
  • Ensure effective use of facilities resources and budgets.

Projects & Administration

  • Support refurbishment, relocation, property acquisition and capital improvement projects.
  • Liaise with internal teams, contractors, consultants and regulatory bodies.
  • Monitor project timelines, budgets and deliverables.
  • Maintain accurate facilities records, policies, procedures and compliance documentation.
  • Prepare reports for management on facilities performance, compliance and risks.
  • Support inspections, audits and information requests.
  • Maintain effective systems for logging and monitoring maintenance requests.

Leadership & Support

  • Provide guidance and supervision to facilities, maintenance and contracted personnel as required.
  • Support managers in resolving facilities-related issues.
  • Promote effective communication and collaboration across teams and locations.
  • Contribute to organisational planning and service development.

Person Requirements

Essential

  • Relevant third-level qualification in Facilities Management, Property Management, Building Services, Health & Safety, Construction Management or a related discipline, or significant equivalent experience.
  • Minimum three years’ experience in facilities, property or operational management.
  • Experience managing multiple sites and competing priorities.
  • Strong knowledge of Health & Safety legislation and compliance requirements.
  • Experience managing contractors, service providers and maintenance programmes.
  • Strong organisational, planning and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience monitoring budgets and managing resources.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and electronic record management systems.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound operational decisions.

Desirable

  • Health & Safety qualification.
  • Facilities Management qualification.
  • Experience in the community, social care, housing or not-for-profit sector.
  • Project management experience.
  • Experience overseeing refurbishment or capital projects.
  • Flexibility and adaptability.
  • Integrity and dependability.
  • Initiative and self-direction.

Role Requirements

The role requires regular travel between Aoibhneas properties and service locations, with the ability to manage competing operational priorities across multiple sites.

Working hours will generally be Monday to Friday; however, flexibility is required to respond to urgent maintenance, compliance or operational matters when necessary.

A full clean driving licence and access to transport are essential.

Employer Benefits

  • 5% employer pension contribution.
  • 22 days annual leave, including two wellbeing days, with additional incremental days in line with service.
  • Access to Digital GP Care and other employee benefits.
  • Access to External Supervision.
  • Employee Assistance Programme.

job.title: Case Worker
job.description:
Caseworker required to work in our Tipperary Offices (3 days Tipp town and 2 days Clonmel).

Monday-Friday 09:00-05:00(on-site)
We are looking for candidates with strong customer service and administration experience.
You will need to drive as you will have to travel for this role

ABOUT TURAS NUA
IPNES supports people who are over 12 months unemployed or employed part-time on low earnings, by providing intensive, targeted and personalised employment support services. The IPNES contract is delivered by Turas Nua, the Irish employability services provider. Turas Nua is wholly owned by FRS Network, an Irish cooperative social enterprise, which has been delivering services to Irish communities since 1980.


PURPOSE OF ROLE
As a caseworker, you will work with clients referred by the Department of Social Protection to IPNES. You will manage a caseload of clients, coordinating our internal support specialists and external organisations to provide a personalised, planned support service to each client, to help them gain sustainable employment. You will also provide each client with one-to-one advice and support to guide their progress towards employment.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop and manage a robust case management plan for each client, working towards sustainable, full-time employment.
  • use our industry-leading assessment technology to identify the client’s goals, ambitions, and barriers to employment. Use the output from the assessment to inform a structured personal progression plan, agreed with the client.
  • Recognise hidden motivations and conflict when assessing clients’ job-readiness, in order to address these with appropriate support and interventions.
  • Provide coaching and mentoring to clients, including providing intensive job search support when the client is job ready.
  • Identify, structure, and recommend training solutions in consultation with in-house tutors, to meet the specific learning and training needs of clients.
  • Fast-track job-ready clients for immediate job interviews brokered by our Employer Services consultants.
  • Maintain strong knowledge of the local labour market.
  • Organise a daily schedule that includes face-to-face meetings, phone calls, online meetings, and email correspondence with clients and other service providers.
  • Work closely with local and national specialist services (e.g., training, literacy, housing, health) to assist the client in their journey towards employment.
  • Present and facilitate workshops and group-learning presentations to clients weekly.
  • Achieve daily and monthly contractual key performance indicator (KPI) targets, managing a caseload of clients; for example, time-bound contacts, assessments, and support activities.
  • Provide guidance and support for more job-ready clients during their initial weeks of employment, helping them to successfully transition to sustainable employment.
  • Ensure that client interactions are recorded accurately on the CRM system.
  • Ensure data protection regulations are fully adhered to.


ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Leaving Certificate or equivalent.
  • Minimum of three years’ experience of working in a customer focused, target driven environment.
  • Strong IT skills/experience in the use of Microsoft office and CRM systems. Must be comfortable with all aspects of remote working technology.
  • Excellent administrative skills – fast & accurate data entry skills.
  • The ability to build rapport and work effectively with a diverse range of individuals both in person and over the phone.
  • Experience in delivering presentations in a group setting or public speaking.
  • Strong prioritisation and time management skills.
  • Fluent written and spoken English.

job.title: New NMBI PIN holders/ DL - Oncology & ED
job.description:
Job Description

Overseas Registered Nurses – Ireland

Position

Registered Nurse – Oncology / Emergency Department / Cardiothoracic

Location: Dublin

About the Opportunity

We are seeking experienced overseas-qualified nurses who are planning to relocate to Ireland and are interested in pursuing nursing opportunities within Irish healthcare settings.

This opportunity is strictly for candidates with recent and relevant experience in one of the following specialties:

  • Oncology Nursing

  • Emergency Department / Emergency Nursing

  • Cardiothoracic Nursing

Candidates must have demonstrable professional nursing experience in one of these specialties. General nursing experience without relevant specialty experience will not be considered.

Candidate Profile

We are looking for:

  • Overseas-qualified Registered Nurses

  • Candidates with recent/relevant specialty experience

  • Nurses who are actively planning to move to Ireland

  • Strong clinical knowledge and patient-care skills

  • Good communication and interpersonal skills

  • Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary healthcare team

  • Willingness to complete any remaining Irish registration or relocation requirements

Mandatory Eligibility

Candidates must meet at least one of the following requirements:

  1. NMBI Decision Letter (DL) holder, OR

  2. NMBI PIN holder, OR

  3. RCSI/registration examination booked

Mandatory Specialty Experience

ONLY candidates with experience in one of the following areas will be considered:

1. Oncology

  • Medical Oncology

  • Surgical Oncology

  • Haematology/Oncology

  • Cancer care

  • Chemotherapy/oncology nursing experience

OR

2. Emergency Department

  • Emergency Department / A&E

  • Emergency nursing

  • Acute and critical patient assessment

  • Resuscitation and emergency interventions

OR

3. Cardiothoracic

  • Cardiothoracic surgery

  • Cardiac surgery

  • Cardiothoracic ICU

  • Cardiac/Thoracic nursing

  • Post-operative cardiothoracic care

Not Eligible for This Requirement

Candidates whose experience is only in general medical, general surgical, elderly care, community nursing, theatre, maternity, paediatrics, or other specialties without Oncology, Emergency Department, or Cardiothoracic experience should not apply.

How to Apply

Please submit your updated CV highlighting:

  • Specialty experience

  • Total nursing experience

  • Current NMBI status

  • RCSI examination status, if applicable

  • Availability and intended timeline for relocating to Ireland

Applications will be screened strictly against the specialty and NMBI/RCSI requirements above.

To know more contact Sonal Tikariha

job.title: Accounts Payable Officer
job.description:
FRS Recruitment is delighted to be recruiting on behalf of a leading and growing construction and facilities management company operating across the Munster & Mid-West region with head office in Limerick.

The Role

You will play a key role in managing the company's purchase ledger function, ensuring supplier payments are processed accurately and efficiently while maintaining strong financial controls.

Key Responsibilities

Accounts Payable & Invoice Processing

  • Process, log and allocate supplier and subcontractor invoices to the correct projects and cost codes.

  • Match invoices to purchase orders, delivery dockets and completion confirmations.
  • Investigate and resolve invoice discrepancies relating to pricing, quantities, VAT or scope of work.
  • Maintain accurate records within the company's accounting and job-costing systems.

Supplier Payments

  • Prepare monthly supplier payment runs for management approval.
  • Process supplier invoices, payments and credit notes accurately and on time.
  • Administer early-payment requests and ensure agreed terms are correctly applied.
  • Ensure compliance with Irish VAT regulations, including reverse charge requirements where applicable.

Subcontractor Administration & Compliance

  • Support Relevant Contracts Tax (RCT) processes and payment notifications.
  • Maintain up-to-date supplier and subcontractor records, including tax clearance certificates, insurance documentation and banking details.
  • Manage new supplier onboarding and adhere to fraud-prevention controls when updating banking information.

Reconciliations & Month-End Support

  • Complete monthly supplier statement reconciliations.
  • Reconcile company credit card and fuel card accounts.
  • Prepare aged creditor reports and support month-end accrual processes.
  • Ensure project costing information remains accurate and up to date.

General Administration

  • Maintain organised electronic filing systems and financial records.
  • Act as the first point of contact for supplier queries and remittance requests.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives within the purchase-to-pay process.

Candidate Profile

Essential Requirements

  • Minimum of 2 years' experience in Accounts Payable, Purchase Ledger or a similar finance role.
  • Previous experience within construction, contracting, facilities management or another project-based environment is highly desirable.
  • Experience using Sage (Sage Business Cloud Accounting preferred) or a similar accounting package.
  • Strong Excel skills including lookups, filters, pivot tables and reconciliations.
  • Good understanding of Irish VAT requirements.
  • Excellent attention to detail and strong organisational skills.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work effectively across multiple departments.

Desirable

  • Knowledge of Relevant Contracts Tax (RCT) and construction reverse charge VAT.
  • Experience with job-costing or purchase-order systems such as LiveCosts.
  • Accounting Technician qualification (ATI), or currently studying towards a finance qualification.
  • Experience with credit card, fuel card or expense reconciliations.
  • Previous involvement in implementing or improving purchase-order processes.

What's on Offer?

  • Pension contribution matching up to 5%.
  • 20 days annual leave plus public holidays.
  • Support for professional development and further study, including Accounting Technicians Ireland qualifications.
  • Opportunity to join a growing and successful organisation with a strong pipeline of projects across Munster.

job.title: Health and Safety Coordinator
job.description:
Health & Safety Coordinator

Location: Tipperary / Midlands
11-Month Fixed-Term Contract | Strong Potential for Permanency
Generous Salary Package

Our client, a well-established manufacturing company based in the Tipperary/Midlands region, is seeking an experienced Health & Safety Coordinator to join their team.

This is an initial 11-month fixed-term contract, with strong potential for a permanent position for the right candidate.

Reporting to the HR Manager, you will support the development, implementation and continuous improvement of the company's Health & Safety management systems across the site.

Working closely with management, supervisors and employees, you will play a key role in promoting a strong safety culture, ensuring compliance with Irish Health & Safety legislation and maintaining a safe and proactive working environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support the implementation and continuous improvement of Health & Safety policies, procedures and systems.
  • Carry out regular workplace safety inspections and audits, identifying hazards and following up on corrective actions.
  • Assist with the preparation, review and maintenance of Risk Assessments, Safe Operating Procedures and Method Statements.
  • Monitor compliance with site Health & Safety procedures and escalate areas of concern where required.
  • Assist with the investigation of accidents, incidents, near misses and dangerous occurrences.
  • Identify root causes and recommend appropriate corrective and preventative actions.
  • Maintain accurate Health & Safety, accident and incident records.
  • Identify & coordinate Health & Safety training requirements across the business.
  • Support Health & Safety inductions for employees, contractors and visitors.
  • Deliver Manual Handling training as part of the new employee induction process and coordinate refresher training.
  • Assist with fire safety inspections, emergency drills and emergency preparedness activities.
  • Assist with the preparation of Health & Safety reports, statistics and performance updates.

About You

  • Relevant qualification in Occupational Health & Safety, ideally Level 6 or equivalent.
  • Previous experience in a Health & Safety role, preferably within a manufacturing, production or industrial environment.
  • Good knowledge of Irish Health & Safety legislation and workplace safety requirements.
  • Experience conducting risk assessments, workplace inspections and incident investigations.
  • Strong organisational, communication and administrative skills.
  • A proactive approach with the ability to work effectively with management and employees at all levels.

What's on Offer

  • Generous salary package.
  • Initial 11-month fixed-term contract with strong potential for permanency.
  • Opportunity to join a well-established manufacturing business.
  • Supportive leadership team and positive working environment.
  • Opportunity to make a real impact on the site's Health & Safety culture.
  • Immediate start available for the right candidate.

If you're a Health & Safety professional looking for your next opportunity within a manufacturing environment, I'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Cath Lab Nurse
job.description:
Job Description

Job Title: CNM1 and Staff Nurse

Department: Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory
Reports to: Nurse Manager / CNM2
Date: 2026

Overall Purpose of the Role

The organisation is committed to providing exceptional patient care within an environment where quality, respect, compassion and dignity are central to all aspects of care delivery.

The Clinical Coordinator is responsible for coordinating, directing and overseeing the day-to-day clinical and operational activities of the Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory. The post holder will work collaboratively with the Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory team and the wider Cardiology multidisciplinary team to ensure the delivery of safe, effective and high-quality patient care.

Key Responsibilities and Deliverables

The Clinical Coordinator will:

  • Coordinate and oversee the daily delivery of patient care within the unit.

  • Assess patient care requirements and analyse workload and staffing needs to ensure appropriate allocation of resources.

  • Assess staff competencies and allocate patient care responsibilities appropriately.

  • Delegate duties and responsibilities in accordance with legal and professional requirements, departmental policies and established standards.

  • Maintain effective communication with the Nurse Manager regarding operational requirements, patient care concerns, staffing issues and incidents.

  • Act as a clinical and professional resource for staff within the unit.

  • Provide direct patient care and clinical support when required.

  • Identify and maintain appropriate internal controls within the department and contribute to mechanisms that monitor compliance.

  • Ensure adherence to departmental policies, procedures, guidelines and internal controls.

  • Undertake other duties appropriate to the role as required.

Clinical Responsibilities

The post holder will:

  • Practise in accordance with the relevant professional standards and the Professional Scope of Practice Framework issued by the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland (NMBI).

  • Maintain a high standard of clinical practice and professional conduct.

  • Promote safe, evidence-based and patient-centred care.

  • Ensure that patient care is delivered in accordance with organisational policies, procedures and clinical guidelines.

  • Support the delivery of high-quality care within the Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory.

  • Escalate clinical concerns and patient safety issues appropriately and promptly.

Managerial Responsibilities

The post holder will:

  • Identify and communicate operational, clinical and staffing issues to the Nurse Manager in a timely manner.

  • Demonstrate knowledge and competence in relevant organisational policies, procedures and clinical guidelines.

  • Ensure that all required clinical and operational documentation is completed accurately and in a timely manner.

  • Respond appropriately to patient and service-user complaints and escalate concerns where necessary.

  • Monitor and contribute to risk management processes within the department.

  • Promote effective communication and collaboration across the multidisciplinary team.

  • Ensure the efficient and appropriate use of human, financial and other departmental resources.

  • Participate in unit and hospital-wide nursing communication processes.

  • Support the Nurse Manager in maintaining effective standards of service delivery.

Supervisory Responsibilities

The post holder will:

  • Allocate patient workloads appropriately, taking into consideration patient acuity, clinical requirements, staff competence and skill mix.

  • Provide direct and indirect supervision to Staff Nurses, Healthcare Assistants and unit reception staff as appropriate.

  • Monitor the delivery of patient care and provide guidance and support to staff.

  • Promote a safe, supportive and professional working environment.

  • Identify and escalate performance, competency or staffing concerns appropriately.

Interprofessional Relationships

The post holder will:

  • Develop and maintain effective working relationships with all relevant departments, medical staff, patients, families and external agencies.

  • Maintain effective communication with the Nurse Manager and Nurse Supervisor throughout the shift.

  • Demonstrate effective delegation of duties and responsibilities.

  • Participate in ongoing consultation and collaboration with physicians and other members of the multidisciplinary team to optimise patient outcomes and achieve unit-specific objectives.

  • Promote effective communication and teamwork within the clinical environment.

  • Demonstrate a willingness to support colleagues and assist with workload when required.

  • Promote a culture of respect, professionalism and collaborative practice.

Quality Improvement and Risk Management

The post holder will actively participate in quality management and continuous improvement processes, contributing to:

  • The identification and review of quality, policy and guideline issues.

  • The evaluation of current clinical practices against evidence-based and best-practice standards.

  • The development and implementation of appropriate clinical and operational standards using structure, process and outcome measures.

  • Hospital, regional and national audit processes.

  • Accreditation and quality-assurance processes.

  • Health promotion and patient education initiatives.

  • The identification and implementation of opportunities to improve patient safety, quality of care and service delivery.

  • The monitoring and review of clinical risks and implementation of appropriate risk-reduction measures.

  • Educational Responsibilities

Under the direction of the Nurse Manager, the post holder will:

  • Develop and utilise effective teaching and facilitation skills within the clinical environment.

  • Participate in the planning, implementation and evaluation of orientation and clinical teaching programmes for student nurses.

  • Provide appropriate feedback to Nurse Managers to support the completion of student nurse proficiency assessments.

  • Contribute to the identification of education and training needs within the clinical area.

  • Identify and contribute to the development of learning opportunities for staff within the department.

  • Participate in the clinical induction and orientation of newly appointed nursing and support staff.

  • Develop leadership skills and act as a positive and effective professional role model.

  • Support staff development through appropriate coaching, supervision and feedback.

  • Take responsibility for identifying and addressing personal learning and professional development needs.

Person Specification

Qualifications

Essential:

  • Current registration with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Ireland (NMBI) as a Registered General Nurse, with registration maintained in good standing.

  • Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification.

  • Current Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) certification.

Desirable:

  • Relevant postgraduate qualification or specialist education in cardiology, cardiac nursing, cardiac catheterisation or a related area.

  • Where a relevant postgraduate qualification is not currently held, willingness to undertake an appropriate postgraduate programme within 18 months of commencing the Clinical Coordinator role.

Experience

The successful candidate will ideally have:

  • A minimum of two years' relevant clinical experience within a Cardiac Catheterisation Laboratory.

  • Demonstrable experience in clinical leadership and coordination.

  • Experience in teaching, mentoring and supporting nursing and healthcare staff.

  • Experience of working effectively within a multidisciplinary team.

  • Demonstrable professional judgement and the ability to make appropriate clinical decisions.

  • Strong critical-thinking and problem-solving skills.

  • The ability to prioritise and manage multiple tasks effectively within a busy clinical environment.

  • Effective time-management and organisational skills.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • A commitment to continuing professional development and lifelong learning.

  • The ability to communicate effectively in written and spoken English, with a high standard of grammar and professional communication.

To know more contact Sonal Tikariha

job.title: Senior Chemist- Waterford
job.description:
Method Development Chemist Job- Waterford

With the onset of new projects /new product introductions, I am delighted to report that a vacancy has opened up for a talented and passionate Method Development/Validation Chemist to join the team of this well- established pharma company in Waterford This company is a much sought after employer a company that is like a big family with a great work culture for all its employee’s and home to state of the art facilities. You will have the opportunity to work alongside outstanding R&D scientists in this company.

Working within the method development and validation team, your role will include analytical method development and optimisation, transfer and validation, according to regulatory guidelines and troubleshooting analytical issues obtained during method development. You will also develop, evaluate & verify analytical methods across a range of techniques . You will also manage analytical/technical projects as well as ensuring all associated data is processed and findings are reported on, therefore cross team communication will be paramount to this position.

You will need a BSc. in an Analytical, Chemical or related scientific field with 4 years minimum experience of working in a GMP facility. You will also need industry experience in Method Validation and experience of the analysis of APIs, raw materials and excipients and the associated analytical techniques that may include chromatographic (HPLC, GC, IC), spectroscopic (IR, LC-MS, ICP-OES, Atomic Absorption), physical properties (particle size analysis) and/or pharmacopoeial testing.

If you want to enjoy a new fast paced challenge and make real advancements scientifically and in your career as an Analytical Scientist/ Method Development Chemist please apply now. This client is already interviewing for the role so I would like you to apply immediately with a CV (Word document format) so as to not miss out on the opportunity.

Keywords: Method Transfer Chemist, Analytical Chemist, Scientist, Chemist, Analytical Chemist, Scientist,Chemist, HPLC,GMP

What we are looking for:

  • Electrical Trade Qualification or Electrical Engineering Degree is essential.

  • Experience with SCADA monitoring and fault resolution is highly advantageous.
  • Strong knowledge of electrical systems, with MV/HV experience highly desirable.

  • Strong IT skills and the ability to work with technical software and databases.
  • Excellent communication and organisational skills.
  • Ability to prepare clear technical reports and documentation.
  • Ability to work independently and manage workload effectively.
  • Flexible approach to work, including participation in weekend on-call duties.
  • Willingness to travel nationwide and internationally when required.

What is on offer:

  • Paid Maternity and Paternity Leave.

You will have responsibility and autonomy for scheduling maintenance for multiple Dairy farms. Our client is one of the largest vertically integrated dairy companies in the Middle East, managing over 195,000 dairy cows across seven modern dairy farms.

The FMM will work closely with farm workshop staff and demonstrate areas of improvement that can reduce costs / improve performance and reduce downtime on equipment. This will be a hands-on role where you will work with a multicultural workforce with a varying degree of ability.

The FMM will work side by side with the workshop team and transfer knowledge to them and help to improve their skills & ensure that the farm staff always keep updated service records.

Please note the ideal candidate for this role will be proficient in reading electrical and hydraulic drawings as you will be the contact for all mechanics when a breakdown arises.

Job overview

To plan and organize assigned farm mechanical maintenance staff so that the broad range of agricultural, industrial and animal feeding machinery and equipment is serviced, maintained and operated in accordance with company procedure. Train staff to ensure that competent and sufficient numbers of maintenance staff are available for the assigned farm sites.

Duties to include

  • To ensure that all maintenance staff are organised, trained and carry out all maintenance in accordance with all company Maintenance and Safety procedures for all farm agricultural, industrial and feeding machinery and equipment.
  • To ensure that all maintenance tasks are carried out in a safe manner and in accordance with company policy and standards.
  • To ensure all workshop buildings and surrounding areas, tools, lifting equipment and electrical equipment are in a clean and safe working condition.
  • To minimise the level of unplanned stoppages of machinery and reduce production losses due to machinery or equipment downtime.
  • To oversee routine and preventative maintenance of all agricultural, industrial and feeding machinery and equipment within the Division.
  • To monitor and assess the performance of all maintenance staff in conjunction with the Farming and Maintenance Manager and recommend training as require.
  • Liaise with suppliers to arrange warranty repairs.
  • Report issues that affect the reliability and running costs of equipment.
  • Arrange OEM training and access to required manuals for workshop staff.
  • Update company manuals that are used for maintaining and servicing machinery. Ensure that workshop staff are always following company manuals for servicing.
  • Identify parts that should be kept in the workshop central store that are necessary to keep equipment running. Ensure that the workshop store does not carry obsolete stock.
  • Navigate different manufacturers parts manuals / systems.
  • Arrange quotations from suppliers for the repair of equipment.

Core competencies

  • Excellent communicator with good influencing and person management skills.
  • A sound knowledge of troubleshooting and diagnostic fault finding.
  • A sound experience with all types of agricultural and mechanical machinery.
  • High degree of confidence and or decision-making capability.
  • Focused under pressure, self-motivated, assertive, confident, fair, and open-minded.
  • Strong IT skills

Candidate profile

  • 5 years year’s + experience in a workshop or service centre environment
  • Experience in managing a large-scale maintenance.
  • Experience with maintenance of large scale agricultural and industrial equipment, and petrol and diesel engine Vehicles
  • Fully operational in the use of structured maintenance systems with a particular emphasis on a planned approach to preventive maintenance and recording and analysing data

job.title: Administrator and Care Coordinator Support
job.description:
Administrator and Care Coordinator Support

Purpose of role

To conduct effective coordination of Care Assistants to ensure that customers receive excellent quality care and support to keep them safe and comfortable in their own homes. A supportive and calm manner together with excellent organisational and communication skills are vital to excel in this role.

Key responsibility

Ensure that Care Assistants are appropriately rostered and allocated to customers so that care is delivered on time, safely and in line with customers wishes (as agreed in their care and support plan), and aligns with the agreed availability of Care Assistants. To strive to achieve optimised scheduling that meets the needs of both customers and carers.

Duties

  • Liaise with the Lead Coordinator and / or Registered Manager to ensure the right number of Care Assistants, with the right skills mixes, are recruited to meet the needs of the business. Arrange cover for Care Assistant sickness, absenteeism or holidays.
  • Accept, allocate and process new customer referrals for care and support promptly and effectively.
  • Process changes to customers’ required care and support needs.
  • Ensure there is sufficient cover to deliver care and support to all customers on time and in alignment with their personal care plans.
  • Monitor the restoring of Care Assistants to maximise efficiency whilst supporting them to maintain an appropriate work/ life balance.
  • Schedule Care Assistants to provide care and support to customers. Work with other members of the Care team to appropriately match Care Assistants to customers taking account of:
  1. Care Assistant skills, experience and availability to safely deliver the care and support plan;
  2. the customer’s preferences and care needs; and
  3. travel arrangements, routes and working patterns to make efficient use of Care Assistant time whilst meeting the needs of customers.
  • Make required adjustments to rotas as required to provide cover for emergency situations, to cover staff holiday or sickness, etc.

job.title: Senior Occupational Therapist
job.description:
SENIOR OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST

Location: Westmeath
Permanent | Full-Time
Private Hospital Setting

I’m currently recruiting for a Senior Occupational Therapist to join a well-established private hospital in Westmeath.

This is a great opportunity for an experienced OT looking to join a supportive multidisciplinary team where you’ll have the opportunity to work across rehabilitation, functional assessment and discharge planning, while continuing to develop your clinical skills.

The Role

As a Senior Occupational Therapist, you’ll manage a varied caseload and provide high-quality, patient-centred Occupational Therapy from assessment through to intervention and discharge.

Your role will include:

• Completing comprehensive Occupational Therapy and functional assessments.

• Assessing patients’ ability to manage activities of daily living and identifying barriers to independence.

• Developing individualised treatment and rehabilitation plans based on patients’ goals and clinical needs.

• Supporting patients to maximise their independence, function and quality of life.

• Contributing to discharge planning and ensuring patients have appropriate supports in place before leaving the hospital.

• Assessing the need for equipment, adaptations and other practical supports.

• Carrying out environmental or home assessments where required.

• Providing education, advice and practical guidance to patients, families and carers.

• Working closely with the wider MDT to ensure a coordinated approach to patient care.

• Liaising with community services and other healthcare professionals where appropriate to support continuity of care.

• Maintaining accurate clinical documentation and reports in line with professional and organisational standards.

As a Senior OT, you’ll also have the opportunity to provide clinical support and guidance to junior colleagues and contribute to the ongoing development of the Occupational Therapy service.

About You

We’re looking for an Occupational Therapist who is:

• CORU registered and eligible to practise in Ireland.

• Experienced at Senior Grade level or an experienced Staff Grade OT ready to take the next step.

• Ideally experienced within a hospital, rehabilitation, acute, older persons or community setting.

• Confident carrying out functional assessments and developing evidence-based intervention plans.

• Experienced in discharge planning and working as part of a multidisciplinary team.

• Comfortable managing a varied caseload and working with a good degree of clinical autonomy.

• A strong communicator who can build positive relationships with patients, families and colleagues.

• Passionate about delivering person-centred care and achieving meaningful outcomes for patients.

Why Consider This Role?

You’ll be joining a well-established private hospital with a strong multidisciplinary approach and the opportunity to make a real difference to patients throughout their rehabilitation journey.

The role offers:

• Permanent, full-time employment

• Competitive salary

• Sign-on bonus

• CPD and ongoing training opportunities

• Career development opportunities

• Supportive multidisciplinary environment

• Employee Assistance Programme

• Free onsite parking

If you’re an experienced Occupational Therapist considering your next move and would like to hear more about this opportunity, get in touch for a confidential conversation.
