job.title: Staff Grade Occupational Therapist
job.description:
STAFF GRADE OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST

Location: Portarlington, Co. Laois
Job Type: Permanent | Full-Time

I’m currently recruiting for a Staff Grade Occupational Therapist to join an established multidisciplinary service in Portarlington.

This is a great opportunity for an OT who wants to work in a role where they can have a genuine impact on the independence, quality of life and day-to-day experiences of the people they support.

The role would suit an Occupational Therapist with an interest in working with individuals with intellectual disabilities and/or autism, and who enjoys a varied caseload rather than a purely clinic-based role.

WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING

You’ll provide a high-quality Occupational Therapy service across assessment, intervention and ongoing support. Your work will include:

• Completing comprehensive OT assessments looking at functional ability, sensory processing, motor skills, cognition and independence in daily activities.

• Developing and implementing individualised OT intervention plans based around the person’s needs and goals.

• Supporting people to develop greater independence in areas such as self-care, daily living, mobility and participation in their home and community.

• Assessing environments and recommending appropriate adaptations, equipment and assistive technology where required.

• Providing advice and practical guidance to families, carers and frontline staff so that OT recommendations can be embedded into everyday support.

• Working closely with a multidisciplinary team and contributing OT expertise to reviews, case conferences and care planning.

• Supporting the development and supervision of Occupational Therapy Assistants.

• Completing clear clinical documentation, professional reports and risk assessments in line with best practice and clinical governance.

• Contributing to Assessment of Need processes and multidisciplinary assessments where appropriate.

• Taking an active role in service development, clinical audits and maintaining high professional standards.

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE

We’re looking for an Occupational Therapist who is:

• CORU registered and eligible to work as an Occupational Therapist in Ireland.

• Ideally has 1+ years’ post-qualification experience.

• Interested in working with people with intellectual disabilities and/or autism.

• Confident carrying out functional and clinical assessments and developing person-centred intervention plans.

• Comfortable providing advice and support to families, carers and frontline staff.

• A strong communicator who enjoys working as part of a multidisciplinary team.

• Organised, self-motivated and confident managing their own caseload.

• Committed to delivering evidence-based, person-centred Occupational Therapy.

WHY CONSIDER THE ROLE?

This is an opportunity to move beyond traditional one-to-one therapy and see your recommendations make a difference in the person’s everyday environment.

You’ll have the opportunity to work across functional assessments, sensory processing, equipment and environmental adaptations, while collaborating with a wider multidisciplinary team and supporting staff and families to put OT recommendations into practice.

The organisation also provides ongoing CPD opportunities, with the role offering scope to develop your clinical skills across a varied and interesting caseload.

If you’re an Occupational Therapist looking for your next opportunity in Laois and this sounds like the type of role you’d be interested in, I’d be happy to have a confidential chat and provide further details.

job.title: Psychologist - Paediatrics HYBRID
job.description:
Psychologist – Children’s Services (Open to both Full time and part time)
Hybrid | Wicklow

A well-established, multi award-winning children’s services provider is seeking a Psychologist to join its growing multidisciplinary team. The service is grounded in strong values, ethical practice and a genuinely family-centred approach, offering children and their families clarity, understanding and practical pathways forward.

The clinic places a strong emphasis on collaboration, reflective practice and creating a supportive environment where clinicians feel valued, listened to and professionally fulfilled.

The Role
The Psychologist will work with children and families as part of a warm, experienced multidisciplinary team. While autism assessment forms a key part of the role, the position is embedded within a service that prioritises thoughtful, ethical practice and positive family experience over volume-driven work.

Key Responsibilities
• Completing autism diagnostic assessments with children and young people
• Administration, scoring and interpretation of ADOS-2 and/or ADI-R
• Contributing to multidisciplinary formulation and shared clinical decision-making
• Preparing clear, compassionate and high-quality assessment and diagnostic reports
• Providing feedback to parents and caregivers in a supportive, respectful manner
• Working closely with Occupational Therapists and other clinicians
• Maintaining clinical records in line with PSI and professional standards

Hybrid Working
This is a hybrid role. On-site attendance is required to conduct assessments with children and families, while remote working is possible for report writing, administration and other non-assessment tasks. The balance of on-site and remote work will support both service delivery and clinician flexibility.

Essential Criteria
• Recognised qualification in Psychology
• PSI registration
• Minimum 1 year experience working with children and young people in an assessment context
• Formal training and experience in ADOS-2 and/or ADI-R (essential)
• Strong clinical formulation, communication and report-writing skills
• A collaborative, values-led approach to clinical work

What the Service Offers
• A supportive, clinician-led environment with strong values and culture
• Genuine MDT collaboration and shared learning
• Flexible hybrid working arrangements
• Administrative support that protects clinical time
• A thoughtful, ethical approach to assessment and family care

job.description:
Discovery & Assessment of Needs Project - Social Care Worker

Location: North Dublin, with some travel to satellite locations
Duration: Approximately 8 weeks
Contract Type: Project-Based / Temporary
HSE Payscale

We are currently recruiting Social Care Workers to join a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) for an exciting Discovery and Assessment of Needs Project within an adult Disability Team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for professionals who are passionate about person-centred practice, disability rights, social inclusion and supporting people to achieve meaningful life outcomes.

The project will focus on gaining a deeper understanding of the aspirations, goals and support needs of adults who use my client's services. The findings will help inform the future development and redesign of adult services in line with the principles of New Directions, ensuring that supports remain person-centred, evidence-based and focused on individual outcomes.

The Opportunity

Successful candidates will receive structured training and induction from the CRC in the assessment methodology before commencing the project. Ongoing support will also be provided throughout the assignment.

Over approximately 8 weeks, you will undertake scheduled assessments with adults attending services.

Assessments will explore:

  • Individual aspirations, goals and future plans
  • Community participation and social inclusion
  • Supports required to achieve meaningful outcomes
  • Unmet needs and opportunities for further development
  • Individuals' strengths, preferences and personal priorities

Requirements

  • Social Care degree
  • CORU reg
  • Irish working rights
  • Have experience working with adults with disabilities
  • Understand the principles of New Directions and rights-based service delivery
  • Have strong skills in engagement, interviewing, facilitation and information gathering
  • Can effectively engage with adults with diverse communication needs
  • Take a strengths-based and progressive approach to disability support
  • Are passionate about person-centred practice, social inclusion and empowering individuals to achieve their goals
  • Share values centred around respect, collaboration, quality and person-centred support

Interested?

If you are a qualified with relevant disability experience and would like to be considered for this project, we would love to hear from you.

You'll be selling instrumentation, consumables, and diagnostics into hospital labs — generating new business, winning tenders, and growing accounts across your patch.

  • Significant experience in sleep diagnostics, including polysomnography and cardiorespiratory sleep studies.
  • Experience working within a dedicated respiratory physiology and sleep laboratory.
  • Excellent knowledge of quality assurance, laboratory standards and equipment maintenance.
  • Strong organisational, communication and leadership skills.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively within a multidisciplinary team.

Desirable

  • Experience with CPAP therapy initiation and follow-up clinics.
  • Previous experience supervising or mentoring staff.

What We Offer

job.title: Senior Radiation Therapist
job.description:
Senior Radiation Therapist

Shape the Future of Cancer Care

An exceptional opportunity has arisen for experienced Senior Radiation Therapists to join a brand-new, purpose-built cancer centre in the Midwest of Ireland.

This is more than a new role—it's a chance to be part of a pioneering team from the beginning, helping to establish one of Ireland's most modern radiotherapy services and delivering world-class care to patients.

Why Join?

As a Senior Radiation Therapist, you will play a key role in developing and delivering advanced radiotherapy services within a collaborative, patient-centred environment.

Advanced Clinical Practice

Work at the forefront of radiotherapy, with opportunities to develop expertise in:

  • Stereotactic Radiotherapy (SRT/SABR)
  • Advanced treatment planning
  • Image-guided radiotherapy (IGRT)
  • Modern radiotherapy technologies and techniques
  • Varian radiotherapy system

Career Development

Commitment to investing in people and supporting long-term career growth through:

  • Clear career progression pathways
  • Leadership and management development opportunities
  • Specialist clinical roles
  • Ongoing professional education and funded training

Research & Innovation

Become part of a service committed to advancing cancer care through:

  • Participation in national and international clinical trials
  • Research collaboration and service development
  • Opportunities to contribute to innovation and evidence-based practice
  • Support for academic development and conference participation

What's On Offer

Exceptional people deserve exceptional support.

A comprehensive package will attract the best Radiation Therapists and includes:

  • Competitive salary plus premium payments and performance pay
  • Attractive benefits package
  • Generous relocation support for successful candidates moving to the region
  • Excellent annual leave entitlement
  • Pension scheme
  • Continuous professional development funding
  • Supportive multidisciplinary working environment
  • Access to the latest radiotherapy technologies within a newly developed facility

About You

You are an experienced Radiation Therapist who is passionate about delivering outstanding patient care and eager to contribute to the development of an innovative cancer service.

You will bring:

  • Significant post-registration experience in radiation therapy
  • Strong clinical knowledge and leadership capability
  • Excellent communication and teamwork skills
  • A commitment to quality, patient safety and continuous improvement
  • Enthusiasm for innovation, education and professional development

Be Part of Something New

This is a unique opportunity to help build a new service, influence future practice and make a lasting impact on cancer care in Ireland.

If you are looking for the next step in your career—where advanced practice, research, leadership and innovation come together - we would love to hear from you.

Emma Fenton is a specialist healthcare recruiter with 20 years experience. Applications and informal contact will be treated in strictest confidence.

job.title: EHS Coordinator
job.description:
Are you an experienced EHS Coordinator with strong Permit to Work and contractor management experience looking for your next opportunity in Cork?

Our client, a well-established manufacturing company based in Little Island, Cork, is seeking an EHS Coordinator to join their EHS team. Reporting to the EHS Manager, this is a key site-based role with a particular focus on managing third-party contractors and ensuring safe, compliant execution of works on site.

What you will be doing:

  • Managing and issuing Safe Work Permits / Permit to Work for maintenance, contractor and project activities.
  • Coordinating and monitoring third-party contractors to ensure full compliance with site EHS requirements.
  • Reviewing method statements, risk assessments and safe systems of work before work commences.
  • Ensuring contractors adhere to PPE requirements, site procedures and controls for life-critical activities.
  • Supporting safety investigations, incident reporting and the implementation of corrective actions.
  • Monitoring EHS performance and driving improvements through site KPIs and action plans.
  • Supporting Management of Change (MOC), safety reviews and the development of safe working procedures.
  • Supporting environmental compliance, including waste and wastewater activities.

What we are looking for:

  • Higher Diploma in Safety, Health and Welfare at Work or equivalent.
  • Previous experience in an EHS / Health & Safety role within a manufacturing or regulated environment.
  • Proven experience with Permit to Work / Safe Work Permit systems is essential.
  • Experience managing and coordinating third-party contractors on a manufacturing site.
  • Strong knowledge of risk assessments, method statements and safe systems of work.
  • Experience within a GMP or similarly regulated environment would be advantageous.
  • Strong communication, organisational and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to challenge unsafe practices and hold others accountable.

What is on offer:

  • Competitive salary based on experience.
  • Comprehensive benefits package.
  • Monday to Friday, days-only role.
  • Excellent career development opportunities.
  • Long-term opportunity with a well-established manufacturing organisation.
  • A key role working closely with the EHS Manager and wider site teams.

If you are an experienced EHS Coordinator / Health & Safety professional with strong Permit to Work and contractor management experience, and are looking for a Monday to Friday, days-only opportunity in Little Island, Cork, apply today with your CV.

job.title: People Change Advisor
job.description:
People Change Advisor - Swords, Dublin

Hybrid Flexibility: 1 - 2 days per week office based.

Permanent Full Time

Salary: €45,000 plus pension, bonus and 25 days AL

Overview:

The People Change Advisor will support the delivery of TUPE transfers, acquisitions, restructures, redundancies, and other organisational change activities across the Ireland and UK business. As the TUPE and Change subject matter expert, you will provide practical advice and guidance to managers, ensuring change programmes are delivered effectively, compliantly, and with a positive employee experience at their core.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Manage a high-volume caseload of TUPE and organisational change projects.
  • Lead end-to-end TUPE transfers, ensuring legal compliance and adherence to deadlines.
  • Coordinate Employee Liability Information (ELI) and mobilisation activities.
  • Support and attend consultation and welcome meetings across Ireland as required.
  • Advise managers on TUPE, redundancy, restructuring, and organisational change processes.
  • Produce redundancy calculations and change-related documentation.
  • Review business cases and identify potential commercial and employee relations risks.
  • Coach and train managers on people change matters.
  • Support employee engagement throughout change programmes.

Skills / Qualifications:

  • Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills.

  • Strong communication, organisational, and problem-solving skills.
  • CIPD qualification desirable.

job.title: Automation Engineer
job.description:
Automation Engineer

Dunboyne, Co. Meath

A leading provider of OT, SCADA, telemetry, and communications solutions is seeking an Automation Engineer.

Join a team delivering cutting‑edge technologies and high‑quality SCADA solutions.

Overview

This role is primarily office‑based, with occasional site visits during deployment and commissioning phases. A major focus of the position involves working with Ignition, a web‑based HMI, SCADA, and MES platform, to deliver a high‑quality front‑end SCADA solution to clients.

The role requires ongoing communication with clients throughout implementation, as well as post‑deployment support for system queries or issues.

Key Responsibilities

  • Presales and design of new solutions and installations
  • Responding to customer and client requests as they arise
  • Liaising with Junior SCADA/Automation Engineers on PLC, HMI, and SCADA software implementation
  • Creating software design specifications and associated documentation
  • Using design tools such as InTouch, Ignition, Broadwin, and 1CC Flexible
  • Training clients on systems once implemented
  • Ensuring consistency of work across all projects
  • Working to project deadlines
  • Managing all files and licensing associated with projects
  • Interfacing with client IT departments regarding security
  • General housekeeping of all SCADA projects
  • Developing standards and specifications aligned with customer requirements
  • Creating standard libraries and productised solutions to improve efficiency in future project delivery
  • Producing work breakdown structures for your own projects and those of junior engineers

What We’re Looking For

  • Strong understanding of SCADA system architecture and components
  • Experience with SCADA platforms such as Ignition, Siemens WinCC, Wonderware, or similar
  • Experience with cloud platforms (Azure, AWS, etc.)
  • Knowledge of industrial communication protocols (Modbus, DNP3, OPC, etc.)
  • Minimum 5 years’ experience developing SCADA and PLC solutions
  • Demonstrated experience in software development and solution design with Schneider PLCs or similar
  • Experience using AI technologies
  • Knowledge of Microsoft SQL Database Manager
  • Familiarity with remote access tools (PC Anywhere, Remote Desktop, TeamViewer)
  • Understanding of data science and statistics
  • Ability to work with VB and SQL
  • Knowledge of Ethernet, TCP/IP, and related industrial networking protocols
  • Awareness of SCADA cybersecurity best practices
  • Experience designing and managing SCADA alarms

job.title: Oncology Inpatient Nurse
job.description:
Key Responsibilities and Deliverable

  • Direct Patient Care:
    • Deliver direct care to assigned patients.
    • Conduct nursing history, summarize data, and identify nursing diagnoses and patient care needs.
    • Observe and record patient signs, symptoms, behaviors, and physiological status; communicate assessments and propose care revisions.
    • Implement individualized care plans for newly admitted patients as per policy.
    • Administer nursing interventions consistent with the medical care plan.
    • Handle admission, discharge, and transfer procedures; assist with patient activities and care.
    • Execute physician orders; safely administer medications and treatments.
    • Notify nursing and medical staff of any changes in patient status.
    • Independently assume responsibility for assigned patient care.
    • Perform specialty service techniques and routines.
    • Maintain aseptic techniques, isolation procedures, and infection control measures.
    • Document all nursing care in patient records.
    • Ensure patient privacy and confidentiality at all times.
    • Evaluate and reassess patient care, revising interventions and outcomes as necessary.
    • Assess patient understanding and compliance with healthcare instructions.
    • Review teaching documentation with the Nurse Manager or designee.
    • Adhere to department internal controls.

Clinical Responsibilities

  • Adhere to The Professional Scope of Practice Framework 2000 (Nursing & Midwife Board of Ireland).
  • Ensure individual patient assessments, care plans, and evaluations are in place.
  • Involve patients’ families and significant others as appropriate.
  • Provide care in optimal clinical environments, following all nursing and hospital policies.
  • Participate in and supervise patient meals and dietary needs.
  • Adhere to visiting time policies.
  • Delegate tasks appropriately based on skill level and knowledge.
  • Record documentation professionally, legibly, and promptly.

Managerial Responsibilities

  • Identify and communicate issues to the Nurse Manager promptly.
  • Demonstrate confidence and competence in hospital policies and guidelines.
  • Efficiently record necessary documentation.
  • Manage complaints effectively.
  • Monitor risk management processes.
  • Maintain effective interdisciplinary communication.
  • Deputize for the Nurse Manager as needed.
  • Engage in ward and hospital nursing communication.

Personal and Professional Responsibilities

  • Maintain a professional portfolio.
  • Utilize opportunities to educate patients and their families.
  • Attend relevant study days and courses.
  • Act as a preceptor or supervisor to students and new staff.
  • Participate in performance reviews with the Nurse Manager.

Educational Responsibilities

  • Enhance learning opportunities in the clinical area.
  • Participate in the clinical induction of new nursing and support staff.
  • Take responsibility for personal learning and development needs.

Qualifications

  • Registered General Nurse license in good standing with the Nursing & Midwife Board of Ireland (NMBI).

Experience

  • Preferably, 1 year of post-nursing registration experience.
  • Oncology experience is preferred.

Job-Specific Competencies and Knowledge

  • Teamwork: Ability to work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and demonstrate motivation and innovation.
  • Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Effective communication, presenting information clearly and concisely, and understanding change management.
  • Planning and Organising: Evidence of effective planning, organizing, and time management skills; flexibility in rotations, rostering, and attitude to work.
  • Knowledge: Recent and relevant experience in the specialized area and acute hospital setting; knowledge of new developments in specialized areas and national strategies in nursing care.
  • Patient Focus: Commitment to quality care, empathy, and treating patients, relatives, and colleagues with dignity and respect.

job.title: Senior Lettings Agent
job.description:
Senior Lettings Agent required for a Dublin-based property developer and operator with more than 20 years of collective property sector experience. The business works across the full lifecycle of an asset, from development and deal management through to letting, property management and financial reporting.

The Role

As Senior Lettings Negotiator, you will play a key role in the lease-up of new residential developments while managing day-to-day lettings activity across an established portfolio. You will work closely with residents, clients, accounts, maintenance and property management colleagues to maintain high occupancy levels and deliver an excellent resident experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage the full residential lettings cycle, from enquiry through to move-in.
  • Lead lease-up activity for new residential developments.
  • Conduct property tours, present apartments and negotiate rents.
  • Manage tenant selection, referencing, onboarding and lease execution.
  • Manage re-lets and ensure vacant units are returned to market efficiently.
  • Carry out rent reviews in line with current legislation.
  • Manage licence renewals and statutory compliance requirements.
  • Conduct property inspections and condition reporting.
  • Maintain strong relationships with residents, clients and landlords.
  • Work closely with accounts, maintenance and property management teams.
  • Provide regular client reporting and portfolio updates.
  • Build relationships with relevant organisations, including technology and finance companies and third-level institutions.
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of landlord and tenant legislation.

Who are you

  • Previous experience in residential lettings, property management or a closely related property role.
  • PSRA Category C Licence.
  • Strong knowledge of the Residential Tenancies Act.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and relationship-building skills.
  • Commercially minded, proactive and solution-focused.
  • Strong organisation, attention to detail and time management.
  • Confident managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Full clean driving licence and access to a car.

Whats on offer

  • €40,000–€55,000 salary
  • Career development within a growing property business
  • Exposure to a substantial residential portfolio and new developments
  • Collaborative and supportive working environment

job.title: Psychologist
job.description:
Discovery & Assessment of Needs Project - Psychologist

Location: North Dublin, with some travel to satellite locations
Duration: Approximately 8 weeks
Contract Type: Project-Based / Temporary
HSE Payscale

We are currently recruiting Psychologists to join a Multidisciplinary Team (MDT) for an exciting Discovery and Assessment of Needs Project within an adult Disability Team.

This is a fantastic opportunity for professionals who are passionate about person-centred practice, disability rights, social inclusion and supporting people to achieve meaningful life outcomes.

The project will focus on gaining a deeper understanding of the aspirations, goals and support needs of adults who use my client's services. The findings will help inform the future development and redesign of adult services in line with the principles of New Directions, ensuring that supports remain person-centred, evidence-based and focused on individual outcomes.

The Opportunity

Successful candidates will receive structured training and induction from the CRC in the assessment methodology before commencing the project. Ongoing support will also be provided throughout the assignment.

Over approximately 8 weeks, you will undertake scheduled assessments with adults attending services.

Assessments will explore:

  • Individual aspirations, goals and future plans
  • Community participation and social inclusion
  • Supports required to achieve meaningful outcomes
  • Unmet needs and opportunities for further development
  • Individuals' strengths, preferences and personal priorities

Requirements

  • PHD/Doctorate level in Clinical/Counselling/Educational Psychology
  • PSI member
  • Have experience working with adults with disabilities
  • Understand the principles of New Directions and rights-based service delivery
  • Have strong skills in engagement, interviewing, facilitation and information gathering
  • Can effectively engage with adults with diverse communication needs
  • Take a strengths-based and progressive approach to disability support
  • Are passionate about person-centred practice, social inclusion and empowering individuals to achieve their goals
  • Share values centred around respect, collaboration, quality and person-centred support

Interested?

If you are a qualified with relevant disability experience and would like to be considered for this project, we would love to hear from you.

Apply now to find out more about this exciting short-term project opportunity.

Call Isabel 0861449043 for more information.

job.title: Payroll / Office Administrator
job.description:

Salary will be in line with qualifications & experience.

job.title: QC Specialist-Biopharma
job.description:
QC Specialist

FRS Recruitment are delighted to be partnering with a biologics company in the Mid -West Region to recruit for a QC Specialist. As the QC Specialist you will be participating in and providing subject matter expertise in equipment qualification, method transfer and routine in-process and release testing within the QC labs, in addition to other QC-supporting activities.This is a great opportunity for an experienced Analytical QC professional that is keen to take a step into a unique role where they will work on a range of projects focused on manufacturing of biological products at early phase clinical trials.

KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Your duties as the QC Specialist will be varied however the key duties and responsibilities are as follows:

  • Participate in method validation and/ or technical transfer execution as needed.
  • Serve as a technical expert to develop, qualify, validate and troubleshoot HPLC, Capillary Electrophoresis, PCR and Cell culture assays.
  • You will ensure all aspects of QC work comply to GMP standards.
  • You will create and approve SOPs, report forms and specifications.

ROLE REQUIREMENTS:

To be successful in your application to this exciting opportunity as the QC Specialist we are looking to identify the following on your profile and work history:

  • Relevant degree in Biochemistry, Biological Sciences, Chemistry.
  • 5-6 years min industry experience working in a GMP biologics facility, specifically in a QC department.
  • Knowledge and practical experience with analytical assays such as HPLC, Capillary Electrophoresis and PCR.

Hours of work : Days only : 8.30am to 4.30pm Mon -Fri


What’s on offer:
• Flexible work pattern
• Yearly Bonuses
• Share Option Scheme
• Pension
• Enhanced annual leave days
• Medical Health care cover
• Dental cover
• Life Insurance
Interested? Apply today!
